note: Rewritten from the redescription (Portuguese) in Rocha & Cancello 2007; the original notes that the soldier measurements were already given in Mathews 1977 and does not repeat them, so no measurements are given under the soldier. The original uses commas as decimal points, changed here to decimal points. The alate measurements rest on only 2 individuals and cover a narrow range.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: The head is rectangular with parallel sides; in profile the dorsal margin is straight from the posterior third to the level of the fontanelle, and from the fontanelle to the base of the clypeus it forms a straight slope. Above the antennal sockets there is a flange-like (ear-shaped) projection, a structure present in this species alone within the genus. In profile the head is not very thick. The labrum is hexagonal. The antennae have eleven segments, segment 1 twice as long as segment 2, the remaining segments subequal, segment 3 sometimes split. The mandibles are slender, long and strongly curved, about one third of the head capsule length, enlarged at the base, each with a tooth on the half towards the tip. The head bears setae, denser in the fontanelle region and sparser anteriorly and posteriorly; the short hairs are denser on the posterior part of the dorsum, becoming sparser towards the front, and are scarce on the venter. The labrum bears 5—8 setae, the apical pair the longest. The postmentum has few short hairs, and the setae are concentrated on the anterior margin. The anterior lobe of the pronotum is covered with short hairs and bears setae on the margins; on the posterior lobe the setae are mainly marginal, with a few short hairs over the whole surface; the remaining thoracic nota bear short hairs and setae, mainly on the margins; the abdominal tergites and sternites bear short hairs and many setae, with a few erect setae on the posterior margin.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: The antennae have twelve segments; segment 1 is the longest, segment 2 is half as long as segment 1, the remaining segments are subequal, segment 3 sometimes subdivided. The head is densely covered with short hairs and setae. The thoracic nota have few short hairs, and the setae lie almost exclusively on the posterior margin. The abdominal tergites and sternites bear short hairs and setae; the last 4 tergites and the posterior margin of all the sternites bear erect setae.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: The head is elongate, slightly concave posteriorly in profile; the compound eyes are large but not very projecting; the ocelli are oval, their distance from the compound eye equal to their minimum diameter; the fontanelle is oval, of medium size and projecting, at the level of the posterior half of the compound eye. The antennae have twelve segments; segment 1 is the longest, segment 2 is half as long as segment 1, the remaining segments are subequal, segment 3 sometimes split. The head is covered with a continuous pile of short hairs, with many setae directed forwards; the labrum has two rows of setae. The pronotum is covered with a continuous pile of short hairs, with several setae over the whole surface; the remaining thoracic nota have very few short hairs, mainly between the wing scales. The abdominal tergites and sternites have both short hairs and setae in quantity, and all the posterior margins except that of segment 1 bear several erect setae. The forewing is covered with short hairs, and the wing scale bears short hairs and many setae. In dorsal view the head has two pale spots above the ocelli and another small pale spot directly above the fontanelle. Measurements (2 individuals, one of each sex, 1 specimen): head length 0.68—0.70 mm, maximum head width (including compound eyes) 0.88 mm, maximum diameter of the compound eye 0.24 mm, interocular distance 0.68 mm, maximum diameter of the ocellus 0.10—0.12 mm and minimum diameter 0.08—0.10 mm, maximum length of the pronotum 0.44—0.46 mm and maximum width 0.66—0.70 mm, minimum length of the forewing (excluding the wing scale) 6.31—7.06 mm, length of the left hind tibia 0.76—0.84 mm.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The soldier is distinguished from all other species of the genus by the flange-like projection above the antennal sockets (the original calls it the only species of the genus with such a projection); the alate differs from the others in the oval fontanelle, which lies further forward.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: The holotype is a male alate (MZUSP 7396, Mato Grosso, Brazil, 12°49′S, 51°46′W, 1967-10-20, collected by A. G. A. Mathews). The original description is in Mathews 1977: 103 (alate, soldier, figs. 45—46), and this entry follows the redescription of Rocha & Cancello 2007. Type locality: Ribeirão Cascalheira, state of Mato Grosso, Brazil, Base Camp, Xavantina-Cachimbo Expedition (12.8145°S, 51.7745°W).
